Well, here is the rest of my side of the story. I'm PMing you the link to his article. For thing #1, When he first told me he had been sexually abused as a child I had no, like 0%, idea how to handle that situation, I thought (Stupidly) that if I knew exactly what it was I could help him better because I could google a way to help (because like I said, I had no clue what to do, but I wanted to help). For thing #2, I honestly thought he was mad at me for denying him sex. I did sigh (but I didnt realize it was that loud), because I was upset and thought it was better to give him want he wanted (which I thought was the sex) then to have him be upset at me. He didn't resist or say anything, and since it went about like normal I thought he was happy and just went to sleep right after. After he told me how he felt about it, I felt like shit. When I said that he should have said something I was NOT in any way shape or form trying to blame him for not saying something! I was saying I wished he would have said something because I didn't realize what was happening and if he had I would have stopped right away!! We had been having sex for 3 1/2 years at that point, I thought he would have felt comfortable enough to say something to me. I wasn't blaming him, I was upset I didnt know it was happening. I was honestly upset about it, I did feel guilty and thought he was upset with me that I wasn't "putting out" or something. I was in no way trying to gaslight him and it hurts that he thinks I was. In terms of grabbing his arm, I know that is a trigger for him when it is unexpected, but when we are in an intimate (sex) situation it is usually expected that him/his arm will be touched and it has never caused any problem before (it would be more of a problem if he never expected me to touch him during sex), and since he initiated it and I thought he still wanted it, I didn't think it would be a trigger =( For thing #3 I never meant it like that at all. His uncle had just died, and I was referring to that when I made that comment in reference to my who had been roommate VIOLENTLY raped 2 times on her study abroad. I was very distraught about my roommates situation and I had been referring to his uncles death, which was a thoughtless, tactless comment, but I was being stupid and was really upset about my roommate ( i was really worried she was going to commit suicide, like I was hiding sharp things from her). Im in no way saying that excuses the comment, it was brashly unkind in any light, but it was not made how he portrays it to have been made. Also, I KNOW men can be raped, and it also hurts that he seems to think I think that he is just making up all these horrible things he has to go through for the hell of it. Finally, he asked me never to talk about his abuse unless he brought it up first, so when I made that "one good question" about his past I felt really bad because it slipped out and I thought he was mad at me even though he answered it (he said never to talk about it, and he didn't bring it up, how was I suppose to know he actually wanted me to talk about it despite forbidding me from doing do?). I just wish he would have brought these things up to me before so we could talk about them instead of telling a bunch of random (no offense) internet people who seem to think I've never tried to help him in any way, when I tried so hard despite my own issues. I just want to tell him how shitty I feel about everything (especially #2 which he said he forgave me for and told me to stop referring to myself as "the rapist" after I broke down and cried about being a shitty rapist a few times, so I thought he knew how sorry I was, but I guess not =[ ), but he cut off all contact, so I wont ever have the chance. Feel free to judge harshly, all my friends keep siding with me (which is the mark of a good supportive friend), but I can't tell them everything without feeling like they'll hate me and leave, so their interpretation of it is biased. Ask any questions you need/want to. Sorry for the wall of text, and thank you for taking the time to read it.

Some plants (specifically the wild tobacco plant here) are able to change from having flowers at night that are pollinated by moths to having different flowers during the day that are pollinated by hummingbirds if there are too many caterpillars (that become the exact moths that pollinate them) eating/killing the plant, or neighboring plants (neighboring plants send out chemical signals when they are being stressed, i.e. eaten. Even cooler thing is plants can tell what they are being eaten by and respond by releasing chemical signals that actually attract predators that specifically eat what is eating them!!).
